type: publisher supplementary data for journal article
title: Identification of the Parameters of the Highly Saturated Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM): Selected Problems of Accuracy — four-quadrant identification workbooks (Supplementary Materials)
rights: The article is CC BY 4.0. The public supplement S1 has no separate license file inside the four-workbook ZIP. This repository supplies factual summaries, selected rounded derived boundary checks and a parser; original workbooks remain at the publisher.
evidence_level: file-level numerical verification across all four workbooks plus primary full text
test: Civilian traction PMSM on a test bench at approximately 550 rpm; shaft torque measured by KTR DATAFLEX 42/200. Paper Eq./figure conventions are separate from spreadsheet column headings.

schema.Arkusz1: One detail sheet in each workbook. Actual d/q currents, voltages, electrical speed, flux, trq calc, T_mes, T_mes_K. Units and sign are explicit in source cells.
schema.DaneZbiorcze: Ten 26 × 26 operating-point matrices. B4 through B274 at increments of 30 identify the measured channel. Columns D:AC have requested d-axis current; rows use requested q-axis current in C. Read measured d/q and torque jointly as finite.
schema.workbook_sign: Across all finite observations T_mes_K equals minus T_mes; the published torque grid agrees with T_mes_K. Compare trq calc with that signed convention.

coverage.partial_cell_example: Q1, requested (130 A, 250 A) has nonfinite measured d/q but a torque grid value of 0. This cell is excluded; interpreting finite torque as a standalone measurement would add one unsupported sample.
coverage.note: Counts include overlapping zero-current axes among the four separately supplied workbooks. They count finite quadrant observations, not distinct setpoints or time samples.

source_check: Both publisher URLs returned the same 1,506,741 bytes. The OOXML workbook relationships, cached finite values, repeated coordinate labels and both sheet representations were checked; signed torque/dq tuples matched to <1e-7 across sheets in every quadrant.
interpretation: The 250 A magnitude in Sec. 3 is a nominal operating envelope. The 20 finite requested coordinate pairs beyond 250 A extend by less than 0.8 A; the measured currents track closely. No timestamp or separate post-limit current request is present, and overshooting a nominal geometric boundary does not establish electronic clipping.

With all 2,084 finite pairs the largest absolute difference between trq calc and T_mes_K is 4.8663641 N·m at Q3 Arkusz1 row 223 (id ≈ −59.993 A, iq ≈ −239.994 A). Only this row exceeds 2.5% of the paper’s nominal 163 N·m. Section 3 describes Fig. 18f as below 2.5%; the full stored workbook range and whatever subset or processing generated the plotted surface need to be reconciled. The signed raw operating point lies inside 250 A.
The article refers to magnetic saturation in the machine, which can alter inductance without command clipping. Steady-state grids cannot be used to infer closed-loop limiter timing.
